evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
Thus, only one satellite is required.
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM) for research and/or education.

criteria.reasoning: Introduction clearly states coral-reef monitoring mission, rationale, single-spacecraft choice and users (CSIRO/BOM, government/university funding), with literature support. Minor referencing quality issues only.

evidence.quote: The proposed satellite will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle – launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport.
The orbit is near-polar and retrograde
An average contact duration of almost ten minutes was achieved
A span of five years is a sound estimate of the useful lifespan

criteria.reasoning: Covers launch site/vehicle, SSO orbit and COEs, ground station, STK access/ground tracks, five-year duration and drag-sail EOL. Evidence is strong, but missing STK files, some technical slips (sunlight, RAAN, EOL manoeuvre) and unbuilt Vega E reduce confidence.

evidence.quote: A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet.
A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle.

criteria.reasoning: Conclusion draws specific conclusions on launch, orbit and ground station and links them to mission benefit. It omits EOL/duration and some claims are generic, but appropriate.

evidence.quote: This report outlines the intended designs and procedures involved in the construction of a Earth observation satellite

criteria.reasoning: Clear engineering structure, executive summary and readable prose. However figures/tables are largely unnumbered, captions inconsistent, bibliography is URL-only, Wikipedia is used, and many table citations [49]-[74] are missing from the list.

technical_issues.issue: Uses Wikipedia [6] as a source, contrary to brief; many in-text citations [49]-[74] are absent from the reference list.
Figures and tables lack numbered captions/titles; Image 3 has no caption.
STK software files are not supplied; only screenshots and an access report are included.
States high altitude low resolution 'is also desirable' (contradiction); 'constant supply of sunlight' ignores eclipse periods.
RAAN 27.33° is described as indicating the launch facility; RAAN at epoch is not a direct launch-site indicator.
Calls EOL the only orbital manoeuvre, but the spacecraft has no thrusters and uses a passive drag sail.
Access table has a duplicate row/access numbering; minor data-quality issue.
Vega E is not yet built; schedule risk is acknowledged but the design depends on it.

overall: Comprehensive single-satellite GBR mission with STK access/ground-track evidence and all major design elements. Technical slips (sunlight, RAAN, EOL manoeuvre), missing STK files, unnumbered figures/tables, and weak referencing (Wikipedia, missing [49]-[74]) lower presentation.
